messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall — latency regression detected for hosted-api (us-west1)
incident-bot: metric p95_tokens_latency increased 2.3x over baseline in the last 5m; alert threshold breached (auto-page). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/api/ops/latency?range=5m :rotating_light:

samira: oncall here, grabbing context. currently serving?

mike: i see the alert, joining. any recent deploys/infra changes to us-west1?

ana (cs-rep): customer-impact: some customers report slow chat responses, CS queue spiked. not seeing widespread errors, mostly timeouts > 2s on long-gen routes.

jordan: tagging product — which routes? chat-complete and streaming endpoints?

ana (cs-rep): primarily /v1/chat and /v1/generate (streaming falls back to non-stream for a subset). p50 shifted ~1.1x, p95 worse at 2.3x.

mike: can someone pull a few representative traces around the spike window (12:12-12:20 UTC)? looking for syscall/schedule stalls.

ana (cs-rep): pulling traces now — will paste spans.

ana (cs-rep): trace snippets (12:15:03 UTC):
```
span 0: request_start -> model_forward 0.045s
span 1: model_forward -> token_emit 1.42s  <-- huge gap
span 2: token_emit -> request_end 0.003s
```

mike: that gap likely in syscall/wait. can we check node host kernel version & recent rollouts? last infra change was a kernel bump on 2024-05-10 to 6.1.12 on canary pool.

ana (cs-rep): hosts in affected pool: gw-usw1-01..04. checking dmesg/boot logs.

ana (cs-rep): dmesg snippet from gw-usw1-02 around boot:
```
[May10 03:12:01] kernel: Linux version 6.1.12-rc1-custom
[May10 03:12:01] kernel: sched: improved cfs patch applied
[May10 03:12:06] perf: interrupt took 3500us
```

perf-bot: perf counters (12:10-12:20): 
```
RQ length avg: 7.8 -> baseline 2.1
context-switches/s: +4100 (norm ~1100)
softirqs/sec: +3.4x
```

mike: those runqueue numbers are concerning — suggests scheduling stalls or bursts of CPU steal. were any container CPU limits changed?

samira: not that I'm aware of. infra says no config changes except kernel canary.

mike: hypothesis A: kernel scheduler change in 6.1.12 interacts badly with our inference runtime (heavy lock contend on worker threads), causing bursts of runqueue and delayed token emission. hypothesis B: garbage collection/backpressure in runtime due to prefix cache invalidations. need logs from runtime thread stacks and top iowait/cpu profiles.

ana (cs-rep): gathering /proc/stack traces and runtime logs for 12:10-12:20 window. pushing to GCS: gs://redwood-incident/1725504321/traces.tar.gz

samira: for immediate mitigation, can we route a percentage of traffic away from us-west1 to us-east1? reduce load on the affected hosts and restore p95 while we triage.

mike: we can do traffic steering via smart-routing. recommend 25% shift initially. also prepare a kernel rollback plan for canary hosts.

samira: doing a manual route update now — 25% -> us-east1 (gradual).

deploy-bot: rolling routing change started by samira: route-policy smart-route-2024-05-12, 25% to us-east1. 30s check.

(30s later)
samira: checking metrics after shift — p95 dropped ~40% on us-west1, overall p95 down 20%. customer complaints dropping.

jordan: good short-term. need RCA doc and timeline to share with execs. let's build timeline in this thread.

mike: timeline so far:
- 2024-05-10 03:12 UTC: kernel 6.1.12 deployed to canary pool (gw-usw1-*)
- 2024-05-12 12:06 UTC: traffic increased due to batch job X (small) + normal load
- 2024-05-12 12:12 UTC: p95 jump observed, automated page triggered
- 2024-05-12 12:14 UTC: oncall ack; initial traces show token emission gap 1.4s
- 2024-05-12 12:16 UTC: routing change 25% to us-east1
- 2024-05-12 12:22 UTC: p95 partially recovered

ana (cs-rep): collecting customer incident metrics: affected requests 126k in 15m window; requests >1s up from 3% -> 29%.

mike: things we need next (action items):
- eng-runtime: collect thread stacks + futex/wait syscalls around the gap (12:10-12:20) from gw-usw1-02/03
- eng-sre: run perf record on a repro host; capture rq length timeline and sched_switch traces
- infra: prepare kernel rollback and gating for deduped canary hosts

samira: assigning tasks: @mike runtime stacks, @ana perf traces, @infra (not in thread) rollback plan. update ticket INC-17255.

mike: quick command snippets to run on affected host (paste results here):
```bash
# check top blocked threads
sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 60
sudo perf script | head -n 200
# check runqueue lengths
cat /proc/sched_debug | grep "nr_running" -n
# check futex stats
cat /proc/sys/kernel/futex_spin_threshold || true
```

ana (cs-rep): pasted perf script top traces (selected):
```
# callgraph
worker_thread [.] worker_poll_loop
worker_thread [.] __schedule
__schedule [.] schedule
__schedule [.] schedule_timeout
futex_wait [.] futex_wait_queue_me
```

mike: futex wait in hot path — suggests lock contention. link to code area in runtime: https://repo.redwood/eng/runtime/src/dispatch/lock_pool.cc (line ~240).

jordan: for customer comms we should note we mitigated via routing and are investigating kernel/runtimes interaction. timeline + next steps, ETA for root cause?

mike: initial ETA for deep RCA 24-48h (need perf samples under load and potentially kernel bisect). short-term: keep shift until rollback or patch validated.

samira: I'll keep routing at 25% and monitor for 4h. if stable, we can reduce after verification.

ana (cs-rep): uploading all artifacts: traces, perf, logs -> gs://redwood-incident/1725504321/ (shared with eng team).

mike: adding hypotheses to thread for post-incident RCA doc:
1) scheduler change in kernel 6.1.12 increases runqueue spikes under our workload, exposing lock contention in runtime -> token emission stalls.
2) runtime lock ordering regression caused by recent refactor + heavier CPU spike leads to futex_wait hotspots.
3) upstream cloud hypervisor CPU steal due to noisy neighbor — lower probability (perf shows local steal = low).

perf-bot: attaching perf flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/1725504321/flamegraph.svg

samira: thanks everyone. good work. filing followups: INC-17255-rollback (infra), INC-17255-runtime (runtime), INC-17255-perf (sre).

(we'll keep this thread as primary RCA coordination — add logs/traces here as they arrive)
